# Case brief — COVID origins

*A synthesis of 2 captured sources on **Where did it start?**. Every quote below is verbatim from a captured source — open the linked source to read it in context. Positions cite their sources by number — the full list is under **Sources** at the end. Compiled with [X-Ray](https://github.com/bryanmatthewsimonson/xray); this is a map of the disagreement, **not** a ruling.*

## Summary

Two camps disagree on the origin.

## Positions

### Lab leak

A research-related incident.

*Held by:* \[[1](https://example.com/leak)\]

### Zoonosis

A natural spillover.

*Held by:* \[[2](https://example.com/zoo)\]

## Cruxes of disagreement

### Does the genome show engineering?

- **Lab leak:** The furin site is suspicious.
- **Zoonosis:** The site occurs in nature.

> No signatures of engineering were found.
> — [The Zoonosis Case](https://example.com/zoo)

*What would resolve it:* An early-case sequence from the market.

## Load-bearing claims

> The lab studied related coronaviruses.
> — [The Lab-Leak Case](https://example.com/leak)
> *Why it matters:* Establishes capability.

## Coverage gaps

- No primary lab records in the corpus.

## Sources

1. [The Lab-Leak Case](https://example.com/leak) — example.com
2. [The Zoonosis Case](https://example.com/zoo) — example.com

---

*Compiled from 2 sources with [X-Ray](https://github.com/bryanmatthewsimonson/xray). No single number stands in for the case — X-Ray maps disagreement and grounds every quote; it does not rank or rule.*
